title: Streamlined credential bootloader and generator adapter: reduce SDK auth boilerplate + ergonomic stream factories (v2.2.0)
author: Elena M. Cruz
release_notes: Introduce a cross-SDK 'credential bootloader' to reduce auth boilerplate; add ergonomic generator/async-iterator adapters for TS/Py and a compact session factory for Go; bump SDK example versions to v2.2.0; no breaking API changes to public client surfaces.
description:
Context and motivation: multiple internal and customer tickets called out repeated auth initialization and duplicated credential-warming code across examples and SDKs. This PR introduces a lightweight, opt-in 'credential bootloader' used by SDK entry points and examples to: 1) perform ambient credential priming (KMS/KV cache warmup) before first request, 2) optionally pre-open streaming channels with a shallow noop handshake to reduce first-stream latency, and 3) provide a small, well-documented helper API to wire credential refresh hooks into existing retry/backoff profiles. The change targets parity and ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs while keeping public APIs stable (no breaking change).

What this PR does (summary):
- Add SDK-level helper: Bootloader.start(credentials, options) with per-language ergonomic wrappers (Python context-manager, TS async init, Go Bootloader.StartWithContext).
- Add generator/adapter utilities: TS provide createGeneratorStream(adapter) that returns an async generator compatible with existing docs; Py provides generator_adapter to convert streaming responses into async generators with built-in reauth hooks; Go adds StreamOperator helper to simplify io.ReadCloser-like stream consumption.
- Wire bootloader into example quickstarts and test harness to demonstrate reduced first-request latency.
- Add new integration tests that exercise warmup paths and stream resume under token rotation.
- Docs: update quickstarts and SDK migration notes; add a short recipe on when to opt into bootloader vs. lazy auth.

Checklist (checked): [x] design doc linked (ENG-9082), [x] unit + integration tests added, [x] example quickstarts updated, [x] API stability review completed, [x] release notes drafted.

Small snippet (Python context-manager wrapper):
"""with Bootloader.start(credentials, warmup=True) as bl:
    client = Client.from_bootloader(bl)
    async for chunk in client.stream(...):
        handle(chunk)
"""

Review conversation (summary, chronological, inline comments preserved in description):
- Jason Nguyen (reviewer): "High level — I like the bootloader idea. Two asks: 1) ensure all warmup behaviour is opt-in and clearly default-off, 2) please ensure the TS adapter preserves backpressure semantics."
- Elena (author): "Agree, defaults are opt-in. Updated TS adapter to return an async generator that awaits downstream pulls to preserve backpressure; added tests that assert we don't prefetch more than N frames."
- Priya Patel (reviewer): "In Python, the contextmanager API looks good but curious about interaction with existing credential hooks — does Bootloader register to the central credential registry?"
- Elena: "Yes — Bootloader accepts a CredentialProvider instance. By default it will use the SDK global provider, but callers can pass an explicit provider. I expanded the docs to clarify recommended usage for services with rotated tokens."
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Go API is idiomatic but change to StartWithContext(ctx, opts) would make cancellations clearer."
- Elena: "Done — renamed helper and added tests for cancellation halfway through warmup."
- Michael Tan (approver): "Tests and docs look good. Approving if CI passes and flaky test is addressed."

CI and test notes: initial CI run failed a flaky e2e when running warmup concurrently on CI runners (test_stream_warmup.py::test_concurrent_warmup) — failure reproduced locally with race in the test harness. Fixed by adding jitter and consolidating the shared temporary directory setup. Final CI run: all checks green (unit, lint, typecheck, e2e warmup). CI summary: unit tests: pass, integration: pass, linters: pass, typechecks (TS/Py): pass.

Backward compatibility and ergonomics: Public client surfaces are unchanged; Bootloader is opt-in and documented as an advanced performance tool for high-latency environments or low-latency streaming start. The generator/stream adapters are additive helpers that simplify typical patterns in examples; we updated the quickstarts to prefer the adapter-based pattern for readability.

Alternative approaches considered: 1) fully automatic warmup on SDK import (rejected because it is surprising and heavy for serverless cold starts), 2) expose low-level warmup primitives only (rejected because it repeated boilerplate in each language). Bootloader is a compromise: small, explicit, and easily mocked in tests.

Post-merge actions and follow-ups:
- Coordinate with SDK maintainers to cherry-pick ergonomic wrappers into backport branches (ENG-9120).
- Monitor first-request latency on canary customers that opt in during the next two release cycles; add metric for 'bootstrap_latency_ms' in Redwood Console (follow-up PR).
- Draft a short blog post / migration note for customers with streaming-heavy workloads.

Merge outcome: Squash-merge to main. Changelog entry added under SDKs for v2.2.0.

If you want to validate locally: run tests in SDK directories (python -m pytest sdk/python tests/integration --filter warmup) and (cd sdk/typescript && yarn test -i) and (cd sdk/go && go test ./... -run Warmup).
notes: Author ran a small local benchmark showing median first-stream latency reduced by ~18% when using bootloader in a 12 concurrent client profile. Benchmarks are small-scale and included in the PR as artifacts.
